newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN GOV'T SELLS 41.657 MLN SHARES IN STATE BANK.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN GOV'T SELLS 41.657 MLN SHARES IN STATE BANK.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry on Thursday auctioned 41.657 million shares in Chiao Tung Bank at a total value of T$2.960 billion.
The shares were sold at an average price of T$71.05 per share, an official at the Taiwan Stock Exchange said.
Prices ranged between T$71 and T$72.

Thursday was the fourth of a scheduled five-day auction during which the ministry planned to auction a total of nearly 418 million shares in Chiao Tung -- a sell-off that would reduce state's stake in the bank to 60.03 percent from 88.83 percent.
Thursday's auction left the ministry with 185.33 million unsold shares for Friday.
Chiao Tung Bank was listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange on September 25, 1996.
The government said in January it planned to release some 800 million state-owned shares worth some T$100 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (July/June).
Listed in the plan was the goal of selling off 634 million shares, or 48.8 percent, of Chiao Tung Bank. The ministry has not given an exact date for the sales.

The ministry said in July that the government's privatisation scheme would accelerate from the middle of 1998, outlining plans to release state-owned shares worth T$450 billion over the next three fiscal years.
